property_summary: After calling sendMoney(address(this), 1 wei) as owner, depositsCount increments in the reference but not in the buggy version.
After calling sendMoney(address(this), 1 wei) as owner, depositsCount is 1 in the reference and 0 in the buggy version.
After the owner sends 1 wei to the contract itself via sendMoney, depositsCount is 1 in the reference and 0 in the buggy version.
After owner sends 1 wei to the contract itself via sendMoney, depositsCount is 1 in the reference and 0 in the buggy version.
After the owner sends 1 wei to the contract itself via sendMoney, depositsCount is 1 in the reference and 0 in the buggy version.

After an initial deposit of 1 ether, calling withdrawAll() sends the entire balance to the owner; the reference contract does so via transfer to msg.sender (owner), while the buggy contract calls sendMoney(owner, address(this).balance), which reverts because the fallback function increments depositsCount but has no receive function, causing the external call to fail and the transaction to revert.

After depositing 1 ether, the owner calls withdrawAll(); the reference contract successfully transfers the balance to the owner via transfer (no receive function needed), while the buggy contract attempts sendMoney(owner, address(this).balance) which reverts because the fallback function increments depositsCount but the contract has no receive function, causing the external call to fail and revert.

After owner deposits 1 ether and calls withdrawAll(), the correct contract transfers the balance to the owner, while the buggy contract calls sendMoney(owner, address(this).balance) which reverts because the fallback function increments depositsCount but the contract has no receive function, causing the external call to fail and revert.

After a non-owner deposits 1 ether, the owner calls withdrawAll(); the reference contract successfully transfers the balance to the owner via transfer, while the buggy contract calls sendMoney(owner, address(this).balance) which reverts because the fallback function increments depositsCount but the contract has no receive function, causing the external call to fail and revert.

After the owner deposits 1 ether, calling withdrawAll() succeeds in the reference contract (balance becomes 0) but reverts in the buggy contract because sendMoney(owner, address(this).balance) fails due to the fallback function reverting when it tries to increment depositsCount during the external call.

After a successful sendMoney call where the target is a contract that accepts ether without reverting, the reference increments depositsCount via the fallback (because it reverts on success so the fallback is not invoked), while the buggy version does not (because it reverts on success).

When a non-owner calls sendMoney, the reference reverts due to the onlyOwner modifier, leaving depositsCount at 0; the buggy version executes the call (to a revert receiver) and increments depositsCount to 1, so address(c).balance differs.

When called by a non-owner with a valid target, the reference reverts due to onlyOwner, while the buggy version executes the call and increments depositsCount; assertTrue(depositsCount == 0) passes on the reference and fails on the buggy version.
Non-owner sends 1 wei to a valid target (self-destructing contract) via sendMoney; reference reverts due to onlyOwner, leaving balance unchanged, while buggy version succeeds and reduces balance.

When a non-owner calls sendMoney with a valid target that accepts ether, the reference reverts due to the onlyOwner modifier, leaving depositsCount unchanged, while the buggy version executes the call and increments depositsCount to 1.

After non-owner calls sendMoney(address(0), 1 wei), reference reverts due to onlyOwner and depositsCount stays 0, while buggy version calls address(0) (which reverts) and increments depositsCount to 1.

After calling sendMoney with 1 wei from owner, the reference contract increments depositsCount only on a successful external call, while the buggy contract increments it before the call even if the call reverts, causing the state variable to diverge after a revert.

After a successful sendMoney(owner, 1 wei) followed by a failing sendMoney(attacker, 1 wei), the buggy contract increments depositsCount on the failing call while the reference does not, causing c.depositsCount() to differ.

After a successful sendMoney to owner (which succeeds) then a failing sendMoney to a contract with no receive/fallback, the reference contract has depositsCount = 1 while the buggy contract has depositsCount = 2.

After a successful sendMoney(owner, 1 wei) followed by a failing sendMoney to an attacker account with insufficient ether to pay the address(this).balance check, the reference increments depositsCount only once while the buggy version increments it twice.
After a successful sendMoney(owner, 1 wei) followed by a failing sendMoney to an attacker contract that reverts on receive, the reference has depositsCount = 1 while the buggy has depositsCount = 2.
